title: Internal Hom quotient annihilation
statement: Postcomposition with the level-n quotient annihilates the level-n ideal-module product of the internal Hom.

source.place: Cohomology of Schemes, Lemma 0882 (lemma-completion-internal-hom, line 6438); the map is left implicit in Stacks and is written out here; the proof there works affine-locally via Lemma 087W (lemma-inverse-systems-affine) and Algebra, Lemma 00MB (lemma-completion-flat) with More on Algebra, Lemma 087R (more-algebra-lemma-pseudo-coherence-and-base-change-ext) for Hom_A(M,N) (x) A^ = Hom_{A^}(M (x) A^, N (x) A^)

proof.text: Write J = I^n, with inclusion ι, and let a_M : J tensor M → M be multiplication. The ideal-module product is the image of a_M. Cancelling its epic image factor proves that image.ι(a_M) followed by f is zero if and only if a_M followed by f is zero (product_comp_zero_iff).

Let q : F → Q be the cokernel projection of JF → F. The cokernel relation and the previous image-factor cancellation give a_F followed by q = 0. Naturality of multiplication gives (J tensor q) followed by a_Q = a_F followed by q. Tensoring with J is a left adjoint by the tensor-Hom adjunction, so it preserves the epimorphism q. Cancel J tensor q to obtain a_Q = 0 (quotient_multiplication_zero). This uses no surjectivity on open sections.

Set H = Hom(G,Q). Under the tensor-Hom adjunction, a_H becomes (G tensor a_H) followed by evaluation. Naturality of associators, braiding and unitors identifies this with the permutation G tensor (J tensor H) → J tensor (G tensor H), followed by J tensor evaluation and a_Q (scalar_tensor_eval). Since a_Q = 0 the uncurried map vanishes. Tensoring with G preserves zero morphisms, and uncurrying is injective, hence a_H = 0 (hom_multiplication_zero).

For h = Hom(identity G,q), multiplication naturality identifies a_Hom(G,F) followed by h with (J tensor h) followed by a_Hom(G,Q), which is zero by the previous step. Apply the image-factor cancellation from the first step to get the required composite with the ideal-module product inclusion. The construction works for all n, including n = 0.
